candidate: C2_r1 (combined package C2, plain B4 rules)
note: Verdicts, reads_as and pairwise verbatim from the blind design-critic (Sonnet); evidence abridged by the author.

reports.reads_as_reason: Boxy head on a very short neck, slab shoulders, an apron-style chest with a hard ledge, thick banded tube arms and a large boxy back pack read as a toy robot, although the pelvis and knee recesses and the white-over-graphite palette are a clear step toward a product.
reports.pairwise_evidence: Narrower waist and hips, dark pelvis and knee recesses, visible neck; baseline fuses chest, hips and thighs into one pillow-padded column. Moderate margin; both read as toys.
top_changes: G1: narrow shoulders and arm thickness, round shoulder tops into the neck (P3)
G2: remove the chest apron ledge, lengthen the neck, rounder head, dark bands only at real joints
G4: one squareness family; round and slim the back pack; smooth the shank steps into one taper (P8b)

reports.reads_as_reason: Box head, bib-edged box chest, ledged block limbs and wide black stripes still read as a stacked-block character, though less than the baseline.
reports.pairwise_evidence: Narrower shoulders, tapered forearms, visible neck, dark pelvis under-structure, thigh taper (P8a 0.485 vs 0.860); silhouette closer to both references (IoU 0.583/0.609 vs 0.526/0.559). Busier: more bands and ledges (S3b 7 vs 3).
top_changes: G6: narrow shoulder/upper-arm mass, lower the chest bib edge, less A-pose splay
G2: one monotonic shank taper, no stacked steps (S3b, P8b)
G4: unify squareness (rounder head, chest, pelvis); thin joint grooves on the arms (also G3)
